page: The Microsoft Azure D32_v4 is a general-purpose instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It runs on the x86_64 architecture and is driven by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. The configuration allocates 32 dedicated virtual CPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache pool. Hardware-assisted cryptographic and vector extensions are active, including AES, AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI for accelerated vector processing.

The instance includes 128 GB of memory, preserving a standard general-purpose allocation of 4 GB per virtual core. Large-block memory reads yield uncached throughput reaching 86.61 GB/s, with write operations measured at 33.96 GB/s. This virtual machine model features no local storage and includes zero integrated GPUs. Workloads requiring persistent storage must attach external network volumes. The omission of local NVMe storage reduces local scratch capacity but allows straightforward horizontal scaling and simplified stateless infrastructure management.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent multi-threaded throughput balanced against lower single-thread execution rates. In stress-ng evaluations, the single-core score falls into the lower 25th percentile at 1412.8, while the aggregate multi-core score reaches 29790.94 in the median tier. Geekbench testing reflects a similar profile, producing a multi-core score of 10337 alongside software compilation results of 22438 points. In-memory operations perform reliably, achieving over 26.15 million Redis SET operations per second and 18.85 GB/s in static web serving throughput.

Given its balanced ratio of processing cores to memory capacity, the D32_v4 offers an efficient allocation of compute resources for horizontally scaled enterprise services. The lack of local storage makes it practical for workloads that rely primarily on decoupled network storage or memory-resident state. Best-fit use cases include enterprise web serving tiers, software build systems, Redis caching clusters, container orchestration worker nodes, and mid-sized database management systems that require stable multi-core throughput.
description: The Microsoft Azure D32_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the instance integrates 128 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It carries no local ephemeral storage, relying entirely on remote network-attached disks, and includes no discrete GPU hardware accelerators. Compute benchmarks demonstrate mid-range multi-core throughput alongside modest single-core execution speeds, complemented by AVX-512 and VNNI instruction support. With substantial memory bandwidth and measured Redis throughput exceeding 26 million operations per second, the hardware resource profile delivers reliable multi-threaded concurrency without resource overcommit. The D32_v4 provides a balanced platform for container orchestration nodes, enterprise web applications, caching tiers, compilation tasks, and relational or in-memory databases requiring steady compute and memory capacity.
